summary: Near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asks His disciples who they say He is, and Peter answers, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
key_insight: The crowds already thought highly of Jesus, as a prophet like John, Elijah or Jeremiah. Peter went further, and Jesus says the answer was not Peter’s own insight: “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but My Father who is in heaven.”
story: Jesus and His disciples went north to the towns of Caesarea Philippi. {Mk} Along the way, as He was alone praying, His disciples joined Him, {Lk} and He asked them, “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?” {Mt}
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.” {Mt} Others said that one of the old prophets had risen again. {Lk}
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” {Mt}

Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but My Father who is in heaven. And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.” {Mt}
“And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.” {Mt}
Then He strictly warned them to tell no one that He was the Christ.
differences: Peter’s answer reads “You are the Christ” in Mark, “The Christ of God” in Luke, and “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” in Matthew.
Only Matthew records Jesus’ blessing of Peter and the words about the rock, the church and the keys.
Only Luke says Jesus had been praying alone; only Mark says the question came “on the road.”
Matthew alone adds Jeremiah to what people were saying; Luke says some thought “one of the old prophets has risen again.”

fit.question: Jesus says, “you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church.” Is the rock Peter, Peter’s confession, or Christ Himself?

points.label: Peter, the first confessor
points.text: Peter’s name means rock; Jesus had given him the Aramaic name Cephas, “A Stone” (John 1:42). Many read the rock as Peter himself, the first to confess Christ and the leader whose preaching opened the church’s door to Jews and then to Gentiles (Acts 2; 10).

points.label: Peter’s confession
points.text: Others note that Matthew’s Greek uses two related words, petros (Peter) and petra (rock), and take the rock to be the truth Peter has just confessed: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God.

points.label: Christ Himself
points.text: Others hold that the rock is Christ, the one foundation (1 Corinthians 3:11), whom Peter himself later called “a living stone” (1 Peter 2:4).

fit.note: Faithful readers differ on the rock, but all agree on what the passage plainly says: Jesus builds His church, it rests on who He is, and death will not overcome it.
fit.short: Peter as first confessor and leader, Peter’s confession, or Christ Himself. Views differ; all agree Christ builds the church.

scene.label: Caesarea Philippi
scene.text: About twenty-five miles north of the Sea of Galilee, at the foot of Mount Hermon, beside a spring that feeds the Jordan. The place had long been a shrine of the Greek god Pan, and Herod the Great built a temple there to Caesar Augustus. Philip the tetrarch rebuilt the town and named it for Caesar.

scene.label: The Christ
scene.text: Christ is the Greek form of the Hebrew Messiah, the Anointed One, the promised King of David’s line. Many expected Him to drive out Rome, which helps explain why Jesus told the disciples to keep quiet for now.

scene.label: The gates of Hades
scene.text: Hades was the realm of the dead, and a city’s gates stood for its strength. Jesus promises that death itself will not overcome His church.

scene.label: Keys, binding and loosing
scene.text: Keys belonged to the steward who opened and shut the king’s house (Isaiah 22:22). Binding and loosing were Jewish terms for forbidding and permitting. Jesus later gives the same authority to bind and loose to the disciples together (Matthew 18:18).

witnesses.matthew: Gives the fullest confession, “the Son of the living God,” and alone records the blessing, the rock, the church and the keys. Matthew is the only Gospel that uses the word church (16:18; 18:17), and here Jesus first promises to build it.
witnesses.mark: Gives the shortest form, “You are the Christ,” and leaves out the praise of Peter while keeping the rebuke that follows (8:33). Early church tradition says Mark wrote down Peter’s preaching; if so, Peter told this story without his own honor. The confession stands at the center of Mark’s Gospel, and from here the road leads to Jerusalem.
witnesses.luke: Sets the question in a time of prayer, as at Jesus’ baptism and before He chose the Twelve (3:21; 6:12). Peter’s answer, “The Christ of God,” recalls Simeon, who was promised he would see “the Lord’s Christ” (2:26).
witnesses.john: Does not record this event. John gives a similar confession by Peter after the Bread of Life teaching: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” (John 6:69).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, and He receives Peter’s confession as the Father’s own revelation. He speaks as the Builder and Owner of the church: “My church.”
seeing.living: Jesus does not let His disciples hide behind what others say about Him. He asks each one, “But who do you say that I am?” Answer Him personally, and rest in His promise that the church built on Him will not be overcome, even by death.
seeing.ponder: If Jesus asked you today, “But who do you say that I am?”, what would your life show your answer to be?

preaching.big_idea: Everyone has an opinion about Jesus; He asks each of us for a confession.
preaching.watch_for: Jesus asks twice: first about the crowds, then, with an emphatic you, about the disciples themselves. In a town named for Caesar and set beside a pagan shrine, Peter’s words about “the living God” stand out.
